title: India Reconstitutes Censor Board With 18 New Members, Including Grammy Winner Ricky Kej
excerpt: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry has appointed an 18-member Central Board of Film Certification for a three-year term, naming actors Suniel Shetty, Pankaj Tripathi and Preity Zinta, filmmakers Priyadarshan and Nila Madhab Panda, and Grammy-winning composer Ricky Kej to the panel that certifies films for public exhibition.
body:
• The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting reconstituted the Central Board of Film Certification on September 16, 2026, with immediate effect, for a three-year term or until further orders.
  • The 18-member panel includes actors Suniel Shetty, Pankaj Tripathi and Preity Zinta; filmmakers Priyadarshan and Nila Madhab Panda; Bengali cinema star Prosenjit Chatterjee; singer Hansraj Hans; and Grammy Award-winning composer Ricky Kej.
  • The appointments were made under Section 3(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, read with Rule 3 of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024. No new certification rules were announced.
  • The reconstituted board will function under chairperson Shashi Shekhar Vempati, weeks after the CBFC held its first full board meeting in six years.

NEW DELHI — The Indian government has overhauled the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), the statutory body that decides which films may be publicly exhibited in India, appointing an 18-member board that draws heavily on the film industry's own ranks.

According to an official notification dated September 16, 2026, the reconstituted board takes effect immediately and will remain in place for three years or until further orders, whichever is earlier. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued the notification under Section 3(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, read with Rule 3 of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024.

An Industry-Heavy Lineup

The new board reads like a cross-section of Indian cinema. Actors Suniel Shetty, Pankaj Tripathi and Prosenjit Chatterjee sit alongside actresses Preity Zinta, Pallavi Joshi and Roopali Ganguly. Directors Priyadarshan and Nila Madhab Panda represent the filmmakers' bench. Grammy Award-winning composer Ricky Kej brings the music fraternity's voice, while singer Hansraj Hans and Gujarati filmmaker Abhishek Jain round out the creative contingent.

The complete roster comprises Vinod Anupam, Manoj Joshi, Abhishek Jain, Ricky Kej, Priyadarshan, Suniel Shetty, Hansraj Hans, Supriya Yarlagadda, Yatindra Mishra, Roopali Ganguly, Preity Zinta, Nila Madhab Panda, Pankaj Tripathi, Prosenjit Chatterjee, Pallavi Joshi, Nishigandha Wad, Waman Kendre and Ramesh Patange. According to Bollywood Hungama, these members will also constitute the board's Revising Committee, the panel that reviews certification decisions when filmmakers appeal.

A Board That Had Gone Six Years Without Meeting

The reconstitution is the first in nearly a decade — the previous board was formed in August 2017. The gap was striking: the CBFC held its first full board meeting in six years earlier this month, where members discussed film certification issues and the functioning of the Revising Committees. The reconstituted panel will operate under chairperson Shashi Shekhar Vempati.

Despite the sweeping personnel change, the ministry announced no alterations to the certification framework itself. The board will continue to function under the Cinematograph Act and the 2024 rules, which govern everything from submissions to the examining and revising committees that screen films. In a separate notice this week, the CBFC addressed concerns raised over the song "Shoorveer" in Mirzapur – The Movie, saying producer Excel Entertainment had agreed to voluntarily replace the song in the relevant sequence — an illustration of the kind of day-to-day certification matters the new board inherits.

Why the Composition Matters

Certification decisions shape every Indian film's theatrical journey — which edits are demanded, which categories are granted, and which films are refused release outright. A board populated by working actors, directors and musicians rather than administrators or political appointees changes the texture of those decisions, particularly at the revising-committee stage, where appealed films are re-examined. The film industry has long argued that certification should sit with people who understand how films are made; this lineup is, in effect, the government's answer to that argument.

The test will come quickly. The coming months typically bring a heavy slate of festival-season releases and big-budget holiday titles, and the new panel's first contested certifications will reveal whether the industry-heavy composition translates into a different approach to cuts and clearances.

The Diaspora Connection

For Indian audiences abroad — in the Gulf, the United States, Britain and Canada, where Bollywood openings draw some of the largest crowds outside India — certification disputes are never distant. The version of a film that clears the CBFC is usually the version that plays in Indian cinemas, and debates over demanded cuts frequently dominate diaspora entertainment coverage of Indian releases. A board that industry veterans help steer will matter to the millions of NRIs whose cinema-going runs on Bollywood.

What's Next

The new members' three-year tenure runs through 2029. The immediate questions are practical: who sits on the examining committees reviewing the next quarter's releases, how the Revising Committee handles its first appeals under the new composition, and whether the early-September momentum — the first meeting in six years — carries into a busier certification calendar.
